note: Session-mode regression cases (typed phrases, one CommandSession per case). Every ad hoc `say` sequence that exposed or fixed a behaviour belongs here. Evidence is checked on a fresh observation after the run.

cases.name: title then body on its own line
replace the whole note
phrases: replace the text with all done

cases.name: follow-up phrase types into the new note
menu command in Chrome
cases.note: Was a known limit (2026-09-22): Chrome's profile picker window ('Who's using Chrome?') was open and is Chrome's key window, so AXPress on File › New Tab, ⌘T through the HID tap, and the strip's + button all left the tab count at 17. Passed with the picker closed on 2026-09-28 (runs/2026-09-28T12-10-14Z) and untagged. Starts from the form page: from Chrome's New Tab page, neither the menu press nor ⌘T opened a tab on 2026-09-29. The executor sends the item's shortcut only when the press is refused, never after a silent press. If it fails again, check for the picker first (`jev-cua ax --tabs`).

cases.name: close a tab in Chrome, not the window
cases.note: 2026-09-28: 'close the chrome tab' clicked the window's close button and the whole window closed (runs/2026-09-28T21-35-37Z): the one-wish merge fired on a clear menu_item (1.00) and let the button (0.58) beat File › Close Tab (0.96). The case closes only the form page its setup opened, from that page: from Chrome's New Tab page, neither the menu press nor ⌘W closed a tab on 2026-09-29.

cases.name: a window's close button, verified by the window
cases.note: 2026-09-28: a window's close, minimize, zoom, and full-screen buttons get one press and window evidence. Before, in a browser the close button was verified by the page text, which the next window's page changed, and a click with no page change was followed by a second click at the same spot. Closing a browser window asks first (destructive 0.53), hence "confirm". Closes only the window the case opened.

cases.name: repeat the last action
cases.note: Notes reuses an empty note, so the repeat verifies through the focused empty body rather than the row count.
